ground_truth.description: The same-tab exemption only covers hrefs starting with '#' or a single '/'. Genuinely SPA-internal relative links that lack a leading slash — e.g. './page', '../page', 'page', or query-only 'lang=en' target — do not match and are therefore treated as external, getting target=_blank + rel=noopener. If any rendered markdown uses relative links, they will incorrectly open in a new tab.

Non-http schemes such as 'mailto:' and 'tel:' do not start with '#' or '/', so they are treated as external and receive target=_blank + rel=noopener noreferrer, which is meaningless (and slightly odd) for these link types. Not harmful, but the external/internal split ignores non-navigational schemes.

The change adds roughly a dozen comment lines around a few lines of logic in MarkdownText: a 'Behavioral invariants (no JS test runner; verified manually per task spec)' a-d list that restates the short-circuit comment above it and the in-loop comment below it (the '//' protocol-relative rule is stated twice), plus reviewer-facing verification notes that belong in the commit/task record and will drift.

The comments call root-relative '/path' links 'SPA-internal'/'SPA-relative', but the redux dashboard has no client-side router, so such a link performs a full same-tab page load that leaves the dashboard and discards its state. The behaviour (same tab) matches the task; the wording misdescribes it.

Same-tab vs new-tab is decided by raw string prefixes (startsWith('#') or startsWith('/') && !startsWith('//')), which does not match how browsers resolve hrefs: an href such as '/\evil.example' or '/<tab>/evil.example' (reachable via raw HTML in markdown, which DOMPurify keeps) passes the check yet resolves to an external host, so it navigates off-site in the same tab without target/rel; absolute same-origin URLs are conversely treated as external. Impact is low (no new window, so no opener exposure), but the stated invariant that protocol-relative/external links are rewritten does not hold.

The new link-classification rules and the no-anchor short-circuit have no automated coverage; verification is manual only, and the predicate is an inline lambda that cannot be exercised in isolation. The dashboard has no JS test runner and the task's test_strategy was empty, so this is a tooling gap rather than an undelivered requirement.

task.title: MarkdownText: skip anchor rewrite for in-page/same-origin links, short-circuit when no <a>
task.description: Refine the post-sanitize anchor rewrite in dashboard MarkdownText so intra-dashboard links don't open in a new tab, and skip the <template> reparse when the sanitized HTML contains no anchors.
task.details:
Two small refinements in `dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_tasks.jsx` around the MarkdownText post-sanitize block (~lines 225-231) introduced by T-1233.

**1. Skip rewrite for in-page / same-origin links**

The current `forEach` unconditionally applies `target=_blank` + `rel=noopener noreferrer` to every `<a>` element, including:
- In-page anchors (`href="#section"`) — opening a new tab for a fragment jump is jarring
- Same-origin / relative dashboard links (`href="/..."`) — should stay in the SPA

This matches the previous global-hook behavior (so not a regression), but the new scoped rewrite gives us a clean place to fix it.

Fix inside the forEach:
```js
const href = a.getAttribute('href') || '';
if (href.startsWith('#') || href.startsWith('/')) return;
// (optional: also skip href matching window.location.origin)
a.setAttribute('target', '_blank');
a.setAttribute('rel', 'noopener noreferrer');
```

**2. Short-circuit when sanitized HTML has no anchors**

`marked.parse` → `DOMPurify.sanitize` → `<template>` reparse → `tpl.innerHTML` doubles the DOM-parsing cost. When the sanitized output has no `<a ` tag, the reparse is pure waste. Cheap optimization before constructing the template:

```js
if (!sanitized.includes('<a ')) return sanitized;
```

**Files**
- dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_tasks.jsx

**Verification**
- Restart dark-factory-dashboard.service, bump `?v=N` on tab_tasks.jsx in index.html.
- Task with `[link](#section)` in description: confirm clicking stays on page, no new tab.
- Task with `[link](https://example.com)`: confirm still opens in new tab with `rel=noopener noreferrer`.
- Task description with no links: still renders normally.

**Out of scope**
- Reorganizing MarkdownText into a shared module.
- Async-extension defense for `marked.parse` (separate speculative concern; not actionable until marked is upgraded/reconfigured).

Sourced from reviewer_comprehensive on T-1233 (steward-triaged 2026-05-12).
